name: Question 1
problem:
Consider the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. You're given that the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ is the unique solution to the initial value problem

$$
{Φ}_{0}^{′}(t)=A{Φ}_{0}(t),\,{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.
$$

A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x(0)$ is presented below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ 

$\text{L2}:\,$ $x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c$ for some constant vector $c$ 

$\text{L3}:\,$ $x(0)={Φ}_{0}(0)\,c$ 

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $x(0)=c$ 

$\text{L6}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}\,x(0)$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L2}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by the 
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L3}$ follows from $\text{L2}$ by 
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from line $\text{L2}$ by substitution from lines {{field-3}}.

Question 1

Consider the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t), where A is a constant square matrix. You're given that the standard fundamental matrix Φ0(t) is the unique solution to the initial value problem Φ0′(t)=AΦ0(t),Φ0(0)=In. A derivation of the formula for the solution x(t) passing through x(0) is presented below.

L1: Let Φ0(t)=eAt

L2: x(t)=Φ0(t)c for some constant vector c

L3: x(0)=Φ0(0)c

L4: Φ0(0)=In

L5: x(0)=c

L6: x(t)=eAtx(0)

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

Line L2 follows from L1 by the
 
definition of a solution curve
definition of matrix multiplication
properties of the determinant
properties of a fundamental matrix
.

Line L3 follows from L2 by
 
differentiating the equation
applying the chain rule
evaluating both sides at t=0
using diagonalization of Φ
.

Line L6 follows from line L2 by substitution from lines
 
L1 and L5
L3 and L4
L1 and L2
L1 and L3
.
